reference: If she reports him, he will lose his comfortable job by Monday.
sk: Ak ho nahlási, do pondelka príde o svoju pohodlnú prácu.
cz: Jestli ho nahlásí, do pondělí přijde o svou pohodlnou práci.
acceptable: If {she|he} reports him, he will lose his {comfortable|cushy|comfy} job by Monday.
If {she|he} reports him, by Monday he will lose his {comfortable|cushy|comfy} job.
He will lose his {comfortable|cushy|comfy} job by Monday if {she|he} reports him.

mistakes.text: If {she|he} will report him, he will lose his comfortable job by Monday.
mistakes.feedback_sk: Po „if“ patrí v First Conditional Present Simple: „if she reports“, nie „will report“.
mistakes.feedback_cz: Po „if“ patří ve First Conditional Present Simple: „if she reports“, ne „will report“.
mistakes.feedback_en: In First Conditional use Present Simple after “if”: “if she reports”, not “will report”.

mistakes.text: If {she|he} reports him, he will lose his comfortable job until Monday.
mistakes.feedback_sk: Termín „do pondelka“ je „by Monday“; „until“ znamená, že dej trvá až do pondelka.
mistakes.feedback_cz: Termín „do pondělí“ je „by Monday“; „until“ znamená, že děj trvá až do pondělí.
mistakes.feedback_en: A deadline is “by Monday”; “until” means the action goes on up to Monday.

mistakes.text: If she reports him, he will lose her comfortable job by Monday.
mistakes.feedback_sk: „Svoju“ sa prekladá podľa toho, komu práca patrí: jemu, teda „his job“.
mistakes.feedback_cz: „Svou“ se překládá podle toho, komu práce patří: jemu, tedy „his job“.
mistakes.feedback_en: The job belongs to him, so the possessive is “his job”, not “her job”.

mistakes.text: If {she|he} reports him, he loses his comfortable job by Monday.
mistakes.feedback_sk: Budúci následok vyjadruje v First Conditional „will“: „he will lose“.
mistakes.feedback_cz: Budoucí následek vyjadřuje ve First Conditional „will“: „he will lose“.
mistakes.feedback_en: The future result in First Conditional needs “will”: “he will lose”.

mistakes.text: If {she|he} reports him, he will lose his comfortable work by Monday.
mistakes.feedback_sk: Práca ako zamestnanie je „job“; „work“ je skôr samotná činnosť.
mistakes.feedback_cz: Práce jako zaměstnání je „job“; „work“ je spíš samotná činnost.
mistakes.feedback_en: A position you can lose is a “job”; “work” means the activity itself.

source_issues: Slovak and Czech drop the subject pronoun of “reports”, so “she” is not given; “he” is accepted too.
